A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main texts, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of four multimodal models, attention probes, and prompting and attention interventions (Tables 1–8 and Figures 2–3).

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds the authors' IsoBench evaluation in Appendix D, Table 9.

M1.justification: The six-interaction framework, two-step prompting and attention-temperature intervention are unchanged. Expanded rule-generation documentation does not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds IsoBench evaluation using paired text and natural visual representations of symbolic content, extending beyond synthetic subject–attribute facts. This is a limited extension covering only vision–text Equivalence; all original synthetic coverage remains.

E2.justification: Baichuan, Qwen, MiniCPM and Phi4 remain the evaluated model set and are reused on IsoBench. Comparator membership in the original experiments, including the three-model probing analyses, is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces an IsoBench comparison with V, T and T+V conditions, extending the original three-modality Equivalence evaluation to a paired vision–text design. Original accuracy metrics, inference settings and probing protocols remain unchanged; IsoBench-specific sample counts and splits are not stated.

E4.justification: Recognition diagnostics, two-step prompting comparisons, attention probes, layer/temperature sensitivity tests and distractor analyses are retained unchanged. IsoBench adds benchmark results without an additional ablation or mechanistic diagnostic.

E5.justification: No new run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates or significance tests are introduced. The five-fold GroupKFold probing setup remains unchanged, and Table 9 reports point accuracies.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds IsoBench results: average accuracy is 58.7% for V, 66.2% for T and 63.6% for T+V. MiniCPM alone slightly exceeds its text baseline, 63.7% versus 63.3%. These are new benchmark results; original Tables 1–8 and Figures 2–3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The interaction definitions and attention-feature construction are unchanged. Appendix B.1 elaborates existing rule templates without adding mathematical results, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about modality interactions, task composition and early fusion. The IsoBench addition supplies supporting evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets IsoBench consistency as evidence that both bottlenecks extend beyond synthetic settings. It also acknowledges that this validation covers only vision–text Equivalence because available benchmarks do not support all six interactions.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly documents one to three antecedent conditions, more than four rules per instance, rule-grounded negative options, and individual/category-level rules. These are additional generation details, not demonstrated protocol changes. Existing inference details and code/data access links are retained.

R1.justification: IsoBench (Fu et al., 2024) is newly cited. The new main-text related-work section largely summarizes positioning already present in Appendix A. The speech-language-model survey's publication update refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v2 adds a main-text related-work summary and validation paragraph, expands rule-generation explanations, and adds Appendix D. Most prose remains unchanged. Headers change to ICLR 2026 publication status, while an Appendix A citation newly renders as '(?)'.

P2.justification: Table 9 is added, with adjustments to spacing, float placement and pagination. Existing Tables 1–8 and Figures 1–11 retain their designs and content; the document is not substantially visually redesigned.

improvement.justification: IsoBench supplies useful evidence beyond the original synthetic setting, and Appendix B.1 improves generation documentation. The gain is limited: validation covers only vision–text Equivalence, sampling details remain unspecified, and the results do not directly validate both bottlenecks as Appendix D suggests. The broken citation is a small presentation regression.
